summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina's Foreign Investment Promotion Agency lists the countries whose citizens do not require a visa to enter — among them Australia, Canada, China, Kuwait, Qatar, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom and the United States — and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs says nationals of EU member states and Schengen signatory states may enter with a passport or a valid identity card. The ministry says citizens of Ukraine need no visa for up to 30 days within two months of first entry, and that Russian citizens may stay up to 30 days without a visa with a tourist voucher, and need a verified invitation letter or a tourist voucher to stay up to 90 days. Citizens of countries under a visa regime may enter without a visa if they hold a valid multiple-entry visa or residence permit issued by a Schengen state, an EU member state or the United States, for single stays of up to 30 days; visas are issued at Bosnia and Herzegovina's diplomatic and consular missions abroad.

conditionalWaivers.text: Citizens of countries with which Bosnia and Herzegovina has a visa regime can enter visa-free if they hold a valid multiple-entry visa or a residence permit issued by a Schengen state, an EU member state or the United States. A single uninterrupted stay may last up to 30 days, with up to 90 days in total in any 180-day period, and never beyond the validity of the visa or permit.

source.name: Foreign Investment Promotion Agency of Bosnia and Herzegovina (Council of Ministers) — Visas: information for visitors

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says landmines and other unexploded weapons remain from the 1992 to 1995 war: highly populated areas and major routes are largely clear, but there is still a risk in less populated and rural areas. It says not to step off roads and paved areas without an experienced guide.

The UK Foreign Office says all foreign nationals must register with the police within 72 hours of arrival, that hotels and some hostels will usually register their guests, and that otherwise you need to contact the nearest field centre of the Service for Foreigners' Affairs. The Government of Canada says that if you plan to visit for 3 or more days, you must register with local police within 48 hours of your arrival.
The Government of Canada says the economy is primarily cash-based and ATMs are limited in rural areas.

Bosnia and Herzegovina's Foreign Investment Promotion Agency says that if you hold a valid multiple-entry visa or a residence permit issued by a Schengen signatory state, an EU member state or the United States, you can enter without a Bosnian visa even if your country is under a visa regime, for single uninterrupted stays of up to 30 days.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Bosnia and Herzegovina?
faq.answer: Bosnia and Herzegovina's Foreign Investment Promotion Agency lists the countries whose citizens do not require a visa to enter, among them Australia, Canada, China, Kuwait, Qatar, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom and the United States; the Ministry of Foreign Affairs says, for example, that US citizens are exempt for up to 90 days within six months from the day of entry. The ministry says nationals of EU member states, Schengen signatory states, Andorra, Montenegro, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Serbia, the Holy See, Switzerland, North Macedonia and Albania may enter with a passport or a valid identity card. It says Ukrainian citizens need no visa for up to 30 days within two months of first entry, and Russian citizens may stay up to 30 days without a visa with a tourist voucher, and need a verified invitation letter or a tourist voucher to stay up to 90 days. Visas are issued at Bosnia and Herzegovina's diplomatic and consular missions abroad, but citizens of countries under a visa regime who hold a valid multiple-entry visa or residence permit from a Schengen state, an EU member state or the United States may enter without one.

faq.question: Can I enter Bosnia and Herzegovina with a Schengen visa?
faq.answer: Yes — Bosnia and Herzegovina's Foreign Investment Promotion Agency says citizens of countries with which Bosnia and Herzegovina has a visa regime may enter without a visa if they hold a valid multiple-entry visa or a residence permit issued by a Schengen signatory state, an EU member state or the United States. A total stay of 90 days in any 180-day period is possible, provided that a single uninterrupted stay does not exceed 30 days and falls within the validity of the visa or residence permit.

faq.question: What currency is used in Bosnia and Herzegovina?
faq.answer: The Government of Canada says the currency is the convertible mark (KM), that the economy is primarily cash-based and that ATMs are limited in rural areas.

faq.question: Is Bosnia and Herzegovina safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office warns of pickpockets and bag-snatchers on public transport and in the tourist and pedestrian areas of Sarajevo and other cities. It says landmines and other unexploded weapons remain from the 1992 to 1995 war: highly populated areas and major routes are largely clear, but there is still a risk in less populated and rural areas, and you should not step off roads and paved areas without an experienced guide.
